newsitem.title: UK: U.S. STOCKS MOSTLY FIRM IN LONDON, MICRON BOUNCES.
newsitem.headline: U.S. STOCKS MOSTLY FIRM IN LONDON, MICRON BOUNCES.

text.p: Most U.S. stocks were firmer in light trading in London as investors awaited another set of economic figures to be published before Wall Street opens, dealers said.
"The market is quietly higher in anticipation of good numbers, especially given the lack of news on the corporate side," said one London broker.
Micron Electronics Inc shares, which lost $7-1/2 in New York on Wednesday, led technology stocks higher, rebounding $1 to $43-5/8.

Among others in the sector, shares in Digital Equipment Corp climbed $1/4 to $46-1/8, while shares in Intel Corp rose $3/8 to $96-3/4. Shares in International Business Machines Corp added $1/4 to $104-1/2.
Dealers said there was little activity elsewhere, as many European investors have backed off U.S. stocks because of the recent rise in volatility.
"The other thing is the currency," the broker added. "The strength of the dollar has made Wall Street very expensive ... too expensive."
Elsewhere, September S&P 500 futures were trading up 2.70 points to 928.50 on Globex at 1041 GMT, while September long bond futures advanced 8/32 to 113-3/32.

Current indications suggest Wall Street will open higher, but the start could be influenced by the consumer price index and weekly jobless claims, due for release at 1230 GMT. Consumer prices are expected to have climbed a modest 0.2 percent in July.
At 1315, data on July industrial production and capacity utilisation will be published. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
